source: Create a 3D level-based speed runner game replacing keys with glowing giant bubbles that play a relaxing popping sound when stepped on. 1. Running Speed Bar & GUI: UI bar that increases player's Speed stat automatically as they run over bubbles. 2. Stage System & Big Win: Divide map into distinct stages with a glowing BIG WIN finish line awarding Win Currency and particles. 3. Multiplier & Rebirth System: Rebirth system that resets Speed for permanent Multipliers and a glowing character aura. 4. Shop & Customization: Shop to spend Wins on Speed Multipliers and custom Particle Trails behind the player. 5. Atmosphere: Bright neon-pastel aesthetics with smooth particle effects on every bubble pop.

image_prompt.text: Wide running lanes chained in sequence through the stages, laid out for continuous forward momentum rather than discrete jumps
A shop at the course entrance where players spend Wins on speed multipliers and particle trails
A glowing BIG WIN finish line closing the last stage
glowing giant bubbles scattered along the running lanes
distinct stages, visually separated from one another along the route

layout_placement.text: Glowing giant bubbles placed along the lanes as pickups that pop when stepped on
The finish-line reward area, awarding Win Currency and a particle burst
stage boundaries dividing the map into distinct stages

notes: No preset was taken: all six Obby presets are built around obstacles and this course has none. The challenge is speed accumulation, not traversal.
The genre route is P6, which validates physics-legal jump spacing - but nothing in this course is jumped, so the generator will be checking gaps the player never crosses.

Four of the user's five numbered systems (speed bar, rebirth and multipliers, shop, win currency) are progression and UI with no layout footprint. Only the stage and finish-line system reached this handoff.

open_questions.ask: Are the stages one continuous run, or separate areas you are teleported between?
How many stages, and how long should each one take at starting speed?

theme: Bright neon-pastel - glowing surfaces, soft particle light, clean and smooth

coverage_missing.ask: One continuous run through all stages, or discrete stages linked by teleporters?
How many stages, and how far apart? Speed multipliers make the right length a moving target.
What happens after the BIG WIN line - back to stage one, or on to a harder set?
How thickly are the bubbles laid down? That is the difference between a lane you sprint and a field you graze.

answers.ask: Are the stages one continuous run, or separate areas you are teleported between?
answers.answer: Make the stages separate areas, with players teleported to the next stage after crossing each glowing BIG WIN finish line.

answers.ask: How many stages, and how long should each one take at starting speed?
answers.answer: Build 3 stages, each taking about 30 seconds at starting speed so the first version stays compact and replayable.
